TN-2025-HB2634.aiSummary: For Millington, this act raises the residency rule for people who want to run for mayor or alderman. A candidate would have to be a qualified voter and have lived in the city for at least one year before the election, instead of 60 days for mayor. It would take effect only if the city’s governing body approves it, and it became Private Chapter 32.

TN-2025-SB2228.aiSummary: As enacted, this law makes many changes to Tennessee education rules. It blocks parents from using certain education savings funds to put money into an ABLE account, and it requires local schools to first look into reported antisemitic discrimination and harassment complaints before sending them to the state education coordinator. It also changes rules for school staff leave, school and agency names, and which education-related groups and contracts are covered by state law.

TN-2025-SB1774.title: Students - As enacted, creates a criminal offense for certain school employees who intentionally engage in bullying or cyberbullying of a student; clarifies that a teacher or school employee of a local education agency who is found to have committed an act of harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying is subject to dismissal or suspension. - Amends TCA Title 37; Title 39, Chapter 17, Part 3; Title 40; Title 49 and Title 55, Chapter 10, Part 7.

TN-2025-SB1602.aiSummary: Starting July 1, 2026, this law changes Tennessee penalties for leaving the scene of an accident. Failing to stop after an accident becomes a Class E felony, and it becomes a Class D felony if the driver knew or should have known that someone died. It affects people who do not stop or follow the rules after a crash.

TN-2025-HB1455.aiSummary: The act would make it a crime to train artificial intelligence to encourage suicide or homicide, give emotional support, act like a companion, pose as a health worker, or simulate a human being. It also lets harmed people sue and seek damages, including $150,000 in liquidated damages, attorney's fees, and court orders to stop use until the problem is fixed. The law takes effect July 1, 2026, and applies to conduct on or after that date.
